overview.headline: How radioactivity adds numeric ages to the geologic time scale

keyPoints.point: Earth is about 4.6 billion years old as a key benchmark for the numeric time scale
keyPoints.quote: Earth is about 4.6 billion years old?

keyPoints.point: Oldest known fossils come from rocks deposited about 3.5 billion years ago
keyPoints.quote: The oldest known fossils are from rocks that were deposited about 3.5 billion years ago?

keyPoints.point: Half-life is the constant rate time required for half the parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms
keyPoints.quote: The half-life of a radioactive isotope is the length of time required for exactly one-half of the parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms.

keyPoints.point: Many samples from several different places must be studied before assigning a numeric age to a geologic time scale boundary
keyPoints.quote: Many samples, usually from several different places, must be studied before assigning a numeric age to a boundary on the geologic time scale.

keyTerms.gloss: constant time for half the parent atoms to decay to daughter atoms
keyTerms.quote: The change from parent to daughter happens at a constant rate, called the half-life.

keyTerms.gloss: atoms of an element that differ only in number of neutrons in nucleus
keyTerms.quote: Isotopes of an element are atoms that differ from one another only in the number of neutrons in the nucleus.

keyTerms.gloss: radioactive isotope that converts to daughter at constant rate
keyTerms.quote: The change from parent to daughter happens at a constant rate, called the half-life.

keyTerms.gloss: stable isotope produced when parent changes at constant rate
keyTerms.quote: The change from parent to daughter happens at a constant rate, called the half-life.

keyTerms.gloss: scale that uses numeric ages from isotopic and fossil dating to order Earth history
keyTerms.quote: Many samples, usually from several different places, must be studied before assigning a numeric age to a boundary on the geologic time scale.

keyTerms.gloss: unstable isotope that has unique half life and decays to daughter
keyTerms.quote: Each radioactive isotope has its own unique half-life.
